full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 27-11-2022, passed by the District Judge, Dhaka, in Arbitration (Revision) Miscellaneous Case No. 554 of 2022, allowing the application, filed under Order 41 Rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for re-admission of the appeal, by allowing the application for condo nation of delay and thereby setting aside the order of dismissal for default dated 18-1-2022 passed in Arbitration Appeal No. 19 of 2003 and restoring the said appeal to its original file and number, should not be set-aside and pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that, admittedly 1.00 acre of land, lying at Plot No. 181 of Mouza Bayel Juni, under Police Station Uttara, Dhaka, owned by the petitioner was acquired by the Government as required by the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha (RAJUK) for extension of Uttara Model Town and the said property was acquired under LA Case No. 2/1987-88. It has been alleged that, no notice of acquisition was served upon the petitioner. However, the Deputy Commissioner has made an award of Taka 15,06,310.80 as compensation for the acquired land. 

 3. The petitioner, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the said award, had filed Arbitration Revision Miscellaneous Case No. 2631 of 199, under section 28 of the Land Acquisition and Requisition Ordinance, 1982 (the Ordinance), before the Joint District Judge (the statutory arbitrator), Dhaka, on which the Deputy Commissioner and the RAJUK were impleaded as the opposite parties. 

 8. Then, almost 4 years after the said order, the appellant filed an application, on 11-6-2017, under Order 41 Rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, before the District Judge, Dhaka, for re-admission of the appeal and this was been registered as Arbitration (Revision) Miscellaneous Case No. 363 of 2017 along with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908, for condonation of delay of 1452 days in filing the said application. 

 12. On 18-1-2022, the respondent was present, but the appellant was not present, nor any cause was shown and the appellate court has again dismissed the appeal for default and the appellant has again filed an application under Order 41 Rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure along with an application for condonation of delay of 293 days and this petition was registered as Arbitration (Revision) Miscellaneous Case No. 554 of 2022. The court by its judgment and order dated 27-11-2022 readmitted the appeal by condoning the delay and allowed the application for readmission of the appeal. 

 14. However, in the meantime an execution case No. 4 of 2005 was filed on 10-2-2005 against the Government and RAJUK for execution of the award dated 26-2-2003 and in that execution case a warrant of attachment was issued on 31-10-2022 by the executing court for attachment of the property of RAJUK, as mentioned in the petition for execution. The said attachment was taken up for execution on 31-10-2022 by the Process Server and the RAJUK gave an undertaken that the decreetal dues of Taka 1,78,20,089.20 should be paid by 13-11-2022 through cheque (Annexure-J). 

 15. Learned Advocate Mr Mohammad Samiul Huq appeared on behalf of the petitioner. He, having placed the revisional application along with the materials on record, first of all submits that, in the background of repeated defaults and condonation of unusual delay committed by the appellant, the appellate court ought to have considered as to whether the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the appellate court on 18-1-2022. The learned Advocate also submits that, the explanation offered as regards the cause of delay was not satisfactory, but the appellate court has condoned the delay of 293 days as well as allowed the Arbitration (Revision) Miscellaneous Case No. 554 of 2022, filed under Order 41 Rule 19 as if it were a matter of routine. He next submits that, the impugned order is apparently a non-speaking order and the appellate court even did not hear this respondent- petitioner before passing the said order. Therefore, he submits that, in passing the impugned order, the appellate court has committed grave error of law, resulting in the erroneous decision impugned before us and that has occasioned failure of justice. He concludes that, this Rule has merit and the same may kindly be made absolute. 

 17. Learned AAG Mr Prahlad Debnath appears for the Government. He has adopted the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the RAJUK. In addition, he also submits that, there was negligence on the part of the Clerk of Government's Pleader (GP) who could not give the date for hearing of the appeal as has been stated in paragraph No. 4 and 5 of the application for Arbitration (Revision) Miscellaneous Case No. 554 of 2022 (Annexure-L). Hence, the GP Office was not aware about the date and they could not appear on the date of hearing. There were no lathes, he asserts, in prosecuting the appeal by the appellant. He finally submits that, this Rule may be disposed of with a direction to dispose of the appeal within a fixed time. He has frankly conceded that, at the time of filing Arbitration Appeal No. 19 of 2003, no application for stay was filed for staying operation of the impugned judgment and order. 

 19. Having considered the impugned order, in the facts and circumstances of this case and in view of the grounds taken in the application filed under Order 41, rule 19 along with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, I find that, the impugned order, whereby the delay of 293 days has been condoned in Arbitration (Revision) Miscellaneous Case No. 554 of 2022 by setting aside the order of dismissal dated 18-1-2022 and restored the appeal is not at all an speaking order. Moreover, when the appeal was dismissed on 18-1-2022, clearly recording that, 

 22. The judgment and order dated 24-4-2019, in Civil revision No. 425 of 2018, been passed in presence of the Government (appellant). It was not passed behind their back and the appellant cannot say that they were not aware or that they needed further notice. It was the appellant's duty to ensure disposal of the appeal within 3(three) months positively. In these circumstances, it was the duty of the Government (indeed the Additional Deputy Commissioner LA) to explain the cause of delay of each and every days in filing the 2nd application under Order 41 Rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure along with an application for condonation of delay of 293 days, which was registered as Arbitration (Revision) Miscellaneous Case No. 554 of 2022. But, the court, without at all recording any reason as to how the delay was explained to its satisfaction, by its judgment and order dated 27-11-2022 has readmitted the appeal by condoning the delay of 293 days (for the 2nd time), as if it were a matter of routine. Moreover, this miscellaneous case was allowed in the absence of the petitioner. 

 23. It was not a matter of routine for the appellate court to allow a miscellaneous case filed under Order 42 Rule 19 by the Government. The Government as litigant remains on the same footing. Yet, the courts usually shows leniency to Government by taking views that the machinery of the Government may take some time in observing necessary formalities in taking steps. But that leniency cannot be extended to give an impression in the mind of the citizen that the courts are making inappropriate discrimination in a case where the Government is a party or are hesitant to pass even a fair, just and lawful order against the Government. 

 24. From the facts and the materials on record, this is found to be a case of gross negligence on the part of the appellant in conducting the appeal and no satisfactory explanation was offered for not remaining present on the date of hearing on 18-1-2022 or about the reason for 293 days of delay (committed for the 2nd time), even after giving repeated directions given by two Division Benches to dispose of the appeal within the time fixed by them. 

 25. Therefore, I find that, in passing the impugned judgment and order, the appellate court has erred in law in passing the impugned order, and that has resulted in error in the decision impugned, causing serious prejudice to the petitioner. On the other hand, in both occasions, by filing two miscellaneous cases for restoration, the opposite party No. 1, Government has put the blame on the Clerk of the learned GP this cannot be a satisfactory explanation. 

 26. The award has been passed by the statutory tribunal and that was competent to pass the same in LA Case No. 2/1987-88, while it is now 2023. By this time, the value of the money has been deflated several times, while the value of the landed property has been increased by several times. Will the requiring body take back the money and return the land? If it does, then the case need not be lingered for another indefinite time at the cost of a citizen who is entitled to be treated equally and in accordance with law. 

 30. However, for ends of justice, the execution case, so far as it relates to the RAJUK, shall be kept stayed for a period of 6 (six) months so that the parties can take steps as per provisions of section 34A of the Ordinance and the undertaking given. 

 31. Before parting of, it is to be noted that, the conduct of the appellant show that it has not come in clean hands or it was diligent in this case. Acts and deeds of the government or of the state cannot be protected to justify any pretended bonafide or to indulge in resorting to unfair practice in releasing the statutory compensation, even in a clear case. 

 The 27-11-2022, passed by the District Judge, Dhaka, in Arbitration (Revision) Miscellaneous Case No. 554 of 2022, whereby the appeal was readmitted and the delay of 293 has been condoned is hereby set-aside.
